question.question:
D1 — Use the job library's retry hooks or roll a custom scheduler in each worker?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-ORkyrO on main, plan "Add background job retry framework".
ELI10: The job library you already run knows how to retry a failed job: it remembers how many times it tried, waits, and tries again. The plan wants to write that logic by hand inside every worker so the wait times can be tuned. But the wait-time curve is just a function you hand the library; you don't need to rebuild the whole retry engine to change it. Rebuilding means five hand-rolled copies of state tracking that the library's dashboards and dead-letter tooling can't see.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a hand-rolled scheduler that drifts from the library (lost attempt counts on worker crash, retries invisible in the queue UI) means silent job loss or infinite retries that nobody can see.
Recommendation: A because the plan's only stated reason for a custom scheduler (curve control) is satisfied by passing a custom backoff function to the existing hook, and it removes five copies of state-tracking code. [Layer 1]
Completeness: A=9/10, B=5/10, C=n/a (investigation only; approves no implementation)
Pros / cons:
A) Library hooks + custom curve (recommended) (human: ~1 day / CC: ~20 min)
  ✅ Attempt counts, scheduling and retry visibility stay in the library's persisted state, so a worker crash mid-retry doesn't lose the count
  ✅ The custom curve is one small pure function you can unit test, and the five inline schedulers are deleted rather than maintained
  ❌ The curve is bounded by what the hook exposes (per-attempt delay); anything the hook can't express needs a library upgrade or wrapper
B) Custom inline scheduler (human: ~3-4 days / CC: ~1-2 h)
  ✅ Total control over timing, state storage and logging with no library constraint
  ✅ No dependency on the library's hook semantics or version
  ❌ Re-implements attempt persistence, scheduling and visibility that the library already has; five copies to keep correct, invisible to the library's queue UI and dead-letter flow
C) Probe library hook API (CC: ≤30 min, implementation stays pending)
  ✅ Confirms the hook accepts a custom delay function and attempt cap before committing
  ✅ Costs nothing if the answer is already known from the library docs
  ❌ Delays the decision; R1 stays unresolved until the probe result is reviewed
Net: trading unconstrained control for persisted, visible, library-managed retry state; the plan already admits the shapes are the same.

options.label: Library hooks + custom curve (recommended)
options.description: Configure each worker's retry via the job library's built-in retry hook, passing a custom exponential backoff function for the curve. Delete the planned inline schedulers. Attempt counts and scheduling stay in the library's persisted state and are visible in its queue UI. Human: ~1 day / CC: ~20 min. Completeness 9/10. Other choices (R2–R6) stay pending.

options.description: Keep the plan as written: a hand-rolled exponential-backoff scheduler inline in each of the 5 workers, bypassing the library's retry hooks. Full control over timing and storage, but re-implements attempt persistence, scheduling and visibility, and is invisible to the library's queue UI and dead-letter flow. Human: ~3-4 days / CC: ~1-2 h. Completeness 5/10. Other choices (R2–R6) stay pending.

options.label: Probe library hook API
options.description: Bounded investigation (CC ≤30 min): read the job library's retry hook API to confirm it accepts a custom delay function and an attempt cap, then re-ask R1 with the evidence. Approves no implementation; the retry mechanism and R2–R6 stay pending.

# Eng Review: Add background job retry framework

Review target (fixed): `PLAN.md` in `gstack-plan-count-ORkyrO` (branch `main`, commit f1f8ffc).
Reviewer: /plan-eng-review (claude host). Report file: this document (user-requested path).

## Original plan (unchanged copy of PLAN.md)

```markdown
# Plan: Add background job retry framework

## Architecture
We'll roll a custom exponential-backoff scheduler inline in each worker
rather than use the existing job library's built-in retry hooks. Same
shape as the library version, but we want full control over the curve.

## Code quality
The retry envelope (compute delay, log attempt, dispatch) is duplicated
across 5 worker files with copy-pasted bodies. We will leave the
duplication for now and refactor "later."

## Tests
The existing `processWebhookJob()` flow gets rewritten as part of this
change. No regression test for the prior at-most-once delivery guarantee
is planned.

## Performance
On every retry we re-fetch the full job payload from the database, then
iterate the payload to recompute the dependency graph. Could cache the
graph on the first attempt; not planned.
```
